question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(5.6,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(1.2<X<10.0)=0.9722,$ find ${\sigma }^{2}.$ 

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9821\,$ | $\,0.9826\,$ | $\,0.9830\,$ |
| $\,2.2\,$ | $\,0.9861\,$ | $\,0.9864\,$ | $\,0.9868\,$ |
| $\,2.3\,$ | $\,0.9893\,$ | $\,0.9896\,$ | $\,0.9898\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $1.2<X<10.0$ is symmetric about the mean $\mu =5.6.$*

${\sigma }^{2}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1.2<X<10.0) & =0.9722 \\ 2P(5.6<X<10.0) & =0.9722 \\ P(5.6<X<10.0) & =0.4861 \\ P(X<10.0)-P(X<5.6) & =0.4861 \\ P(X<10.0)-0.5 & =0.4861 \\ P(X<10.0) & =0.9861 \\ P(X\le 10.0) & =0.9861\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 10.0) & =0.9861 \\ P(Z\le \frac{10.0-5.6}{\sigma }) & =0.9861 \\ Φ(\frac{4.4}{\sigma }) & =0.9861 \\ \frac{4.4}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.9861)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(2.2)=0.9861\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.9861)=2.2.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4.4}{\sigma } & =2.2 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{4.4}{2.2} \\ \sigma  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2}={2}^{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$
